text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Democratic Alliance Party alleged that the ruling Democratic Party financed its May 26 general election campaign with money from pyramid schemes. The Democratic Party has denied the allegations.
- The key opposition Socialists have backed a recent strike by students and workers, supported by Azem Hajdari, a ruling Democrat rival turned unionist leader.
- Greek police have arrested a number of Albanian immigrants after a series of burglaries by an Albanian ring in an Athens suburb sparked outrage among residents.
- Albania has sent a delegation to Greece to speed up the transfer of 200 out of 700 Albanians convicts serving jail terms in Greece.
- Italy has given legal status to about 40,000 Albanian immigrants in seven months.
- A parliamentary commission has begun investigating pyramid schemes which have mushroomed all over the country.
- The Silva company, which has a concession of bitumen sands and a scheme offering a return of 11 percent a month on investments, cut its interest rate to 7.5 percent from Tuesday.
- The Albanian government has caused mayhem in traders calculations by making unannounced changes to customs tariffs.

- Contaminated water has caused health disorders among 260 people in the southern mining town of Memaliaj. The Health Ministry has closed down the aqueduct which supplies the town, leaving 10,000 people without water.
- Patrols will start after midnight to shoot stray animals in Tirana streets, with one dollar paid for every animal killed.
- Albania will pass a law on the control of independent televisions in January.
- Vefa, the country's biggest concern which also runs a scheme offering a return of eight percent a month on investments, said it would lower its interest rate to five percent a month.

- An Albanian senior energy official has told Italy's ENEL and SNAM companies Albania would be ready to install on its western shore a refinery of Nigerian gas refused by the inhabitants of Montefalcone in Italy.
